draft.title: Linear dependence
card: Vectors are linearly dependent if one of them can be built from the others by scaling and adding. Otherwise they are linearly independent.
Two vectors are dependent when one is a scalar multiple of the other, so they are parallel. For example, (1, 2, 3) and (2, 4, 6) are dependent, because the second is 2 times the first.
Three vectors are dependent if one is a combination of the other two, so all three lie in the same plane. Check by trying to write one as a combination of the other two.
In 3D, three independent vectors point in genuinely different directions and do not share a plane. A set of four or more vectors in 3D is always dependent.
draft.remember: Dependent means one vector is made from the others. Independent vectors each add a new direction.

a.q: Which pair of vectors is linearly dependent?
a.why: (−2, 4, −6) is −2 times (1, −2, 3), so the two are parallel. In (2, 4, 6) the signs do not match a single multiple, so it is not a multiple of (1, −2, 3), even though the numbers look related.
a.clue: Look for one number that scales every component of the first vector.

b.q: Let a = (1, 0, 0), b = (0, 1, 0) and c = (2, 3, 0). Which statement is correct?
opts: The three are dependent, as c = 2a + 3b
The three are independent, as no two are parallel
The three are independent, as they have three components
The three are dependent, as c is a multiple of a
b.why: c = 2a + 3b, so c is built from a and b and the set is dependent. No two vectors are parallel, but that alone does not make three vectors independent: all three lie in the plane z = 0.
b.clue: Try to build c from a and b by scaling and adding.

b.best: The three are dependent, as c = 2a + 3b
